properties.title: Abstract Security for Microsoft Sentinel: one-deploy solution

steps.name: basics
steps.label: Basics
steps.description: **Abstract Security for Microsoft Sentinel: one-deploy solution** Abstract Security: a security data pipeline and agentic SIEM in one platform. One Azure deployment that creates the Data Collection Endpoint, Data Collection Rule and tables that Abstract Security sends events to through the Logs Ingestion API, and installs Microsoft Sentinel content for that data. **Abstract Security for Microsoft Sentinel** sets up, in one deployment, everything Abstract needs to deliver data into Microsoft Sentinel. Choose the resource group that holds your Sentinel workspace, or a new one. Every field below explains what it sets, when to change it and what follows.

location.label: Region
location.toolTip: What: the region of a new workspace and of the Data Collection Endpoint and Rule. With an existing workspace, the endpoint and rule follow the workspace's region whatever is chosen here.

options.text: One deployment sets up everything Abstract needs to deliver data into Microsoft Sentinel: the Log Analytics workspace (new or yours), the Data Collection Endpoint and Rule Abstract sends to, the AbstractEventLogs_CL table, optional routes into Microsoft's ASIM tables, a data-lake table and vendor tables, and the Abstract content package (data connector tile, parser, analytics rules, hunting queries, workbooks, playbooks and automation rules). Have ready: Contributor and User Access Administrator (or Owner) on the resource group, and the Abstract app registration if Abstract has already given you one.

body.query: [concat('resources | where subscriptionId =~ "', steps('basics').resourceScope.subscription.subscriptionId, '" and type =~ "microsoft.operationalinsights/workspaces" and resourceGroup =~ "', steps('basics').resourceScope.resourceGroup.name, '" | project name, location, id = tolower(id), retention = toint(properties.retentionInDays), sku = tostring(properties.sku.name) | join kind=leftouter (resources | where type =~ "microsoft.operationsmanagement/solutions" and name startswith "SecurityInsights(" | project id = tolower(tostring(properties.workspaceResourceId)), hasSentinel = 1) on id | extend sentinel = iff(isnotnull(hasSentinel), "yes", "no") | project name, location, retention, sku, sentinel | order by name asc')]

elements.name: workspaceMode
elements.label: Log Analytics workspace
elements.toolTip: What: the Microsoft Sentinel workspace Abstract writes to. When: choose 'Create new' for a fresh workspace with Microsoft Sentinel switched on; choose 'Use existing' to add Abstract to a workspace that already runs Microsoft Sentinel. Consequence: an existing workspace is never modified (its retention, pricing tier and other tables are left alone). It must be in the resource group chosen above. Find yours: Azure portal > Microsoft Sentinel > the workspace > Overview > Resource group.

elements.name: workspaceNameNew
elements.label: New workspace name
elements.toolTip: What: the name of the new Log Analytics workspace. When: leave empty and the deployment names it abstract-sentinel-<unique suffix>. Consequence: the name cannot be changed later. 4 to 63 letters, digits and hyphens. The form checks it against the workspaces already in this resource group.

validations.message: 4 to 63 letters, digits and hyphens, starting and ending with a letter or digit.
A workspace with this name is already in this resource group. Choose 'Use existing' instead, or pick another name: creating it again would update that workspace.

elements.name: workspaceRetentionDays
elements.label: Retention of the new workspace
elements.toolTip: What: how long the new workspace keeps data in its interactive (Analytics) tier. When: 90 days is included in the Microsoft Sentinel price; longer costs per GB per month. Consequence: applies to the new workspace only; change it later in Log Analytics workspace > Usage and estimated costs > Data retention.

elements.name: workspaceExisting
elements.label: Existing Microsoft Sentinel workspace
elements.toolTip: What: the workspaces in this resource group that run Microsoft Sentinel, read live from Azure Resource Graph (a workspace counts when its SecurityInsights solution exists). When: pick the workspace your SOC uses. Consequence: the Data Collection Endpoint and Rule are created in this workspace's region, and Abstract's tables and content are added to it. Nothing else in it changes. Not listed? It is in another resource group (start again and choose that group) or Microsoft Sentinel is not on (Microsoft Sentinel > Create > the workspace > Add).

elements.name: tags
elements.toolTip: What: tags (name and value) put on every resource this deployment creates that supports tags: the new workspace, the Data Collection Endpoint and Rule, the tables' parent resources, the playbooks and their API connections. When: add the tags your cost or ownership policy requires. Consequence: an existing workspace keeps its own tags. Portal: each created resource > Tags.

options.text: Questions or help with this deployment: email support@abstract.security or use the contact page at https://www.abstract.security/contact-us.

Abstract sends data as a Microsoft Entra ID app registration through the Logs Ingestion API. The deployment gives that app's service principal one role, Monitoring Metrics Publisher, on the Data Collection Rule only: nothing on the workspace, the subscription or any other resource. Afterwards, enter the app's Application (client) ID, a client secret and your tenant ID in the Abstract Azure Sentinel Destination.

elements.name: appMode
elements.label: How to identify the Abstract app
elements.toolTip: What: how the form finds the app that will be allowed to send data. When: 'Pick or register' searches your app registrations (or registers a new one); 'Enter the Object ID' is for an app you cannot search for, such as a multitenant app Abstract provides; 'Skip' leaves the grant for later. Consequence: 'Skip' deploys everything except the role assignment, and no data arrives until someone grants Monitoring Metrics Publisher on the Data Collection Rule to the app. Portal: Microsoft Entra ID > Enterprise applications.

label.password: Client secret (not used by this deployment)

toolTip.password: The selector always asks for a credential. This template does not read it and does not store it. Create the app's client secret in Microsoft Entra ID > App registrations > the app > Certificates & secrets, and enter it in Abstract, not here.
toolTip.authenticationType: Not used by this template; leave Password.

options.text: No app is selected yet. Select 'Change selection' to search your app registrations or register a new one. If you continue without one, the deployment skips the role grant.

[concat('Selected app: Application (client) ID ', coalesce(steps('app').sp.appId, ''), ', service principal Object ID ', coalesce(first(steps('app').sp.objectId), ''), '. The deployment grants Monitoring Metrics Publisher on the Data Collection Rule to this Object ID. Enter the Application (client) ID in Abstract.')]

elements.name: principalIdManual
elements.label: Service principal Object ID
elements.toolTip: What: the Object ID of the app's service principal (its enterprise application), not the Application (client) ID. Find it: Microsoft Entra ID > Enterprise applications > the Abstract app > Overview > Object ID, or in Cloud Shell: az ad sp show --id <application-client-id> --query id -o tsv. Consequence: a wrong ID either fails the deployment (no such principal) or grants the role to the wrong identity. When: the app cannot be found with the picker, or Abstract gave you an Object ID.

body.query: [concat('resources | where subscriptionId =~ "', steps('basics').resourceScope.subscription.subscriptionId, '" and resourceGroup =~ "', steps('basics').resourceScope.resourceGroup.name, '" and type in~ ("microsoft.insights/datacollectionendpoints", "microsoft.insights/datacollectionrules") | project name, location, dcKind = iff(type =~ "microsoft.insights/datacollectionendpoints", "dce", "dcr"), isAbstract = iff(isnotnull(properties.streamDeclarations["Custom-AbstractEventLogs_CL"]), "yes", "no"), flows = coalesce(array_length(properties.dataFlows), 0) | order by name asc')]

options.text: Abstract sends every event to one Data Collection Rule (DCR) through one Data Collection Endpoint (DCE). The rule's transformation decides which table each event lands in. Both are created in the workspace's region. Their names are listed live from this resource group, so a clash is caught here and not at deployment time.

elements.name: dceMode
elements.label: Data Collection Endpoint
elements.toolTip: What: the HTTPS endpoint Abstract posts events to. When: 'Create new' for a first install; 'Use existing' to re-run over the endpoint an earlier run created. Consequence: choosing an existing endpoint re-applies this template's settings to it (public network access Enabled, these tags); other rules that use it keep working. Portal: Monitor > Settings > Data Collection Endpoints.

elements.name: dceNameNew
elements.label: New endpoint name
elements.toolTip: What: the name of the new Data Collection Endpoint. Consequence: the endpoint's URL, which you enter in Abstract, is derived from it. 3 to 44 letters, digits and hyphens. When: a first install. Portal: Monitor > Settings > Data Collection Endpoints.

validations.message: An endpoint with this name is already in this resource group, so deploying would overwrite its settings. Choose 'Use existing' to do that on purpose, or pick another name.

elements.name: dceExisting
elements.label: Existing endpoint
elements.toolTip: What: the Data Collection Endpoints in this resource group, read live. Consequence: the deployment re-applies its settings and keeps its URL. It must be in the workspace's region. When: re-running over an endpoint an earlier run created. Portal: Monitor > Settings > Data Collection Endpoints.

elements.name: dcrMode
elements.label: Data Collection Rule
elements.toolTip: What: the rule that receives Abstract's stream (Custom-AbstractEventLogs_CL) and routes each event to its table. When: 'Create new' for a first install; 'Use existing' only for a rule an earlier run of this solution created. Consequence: deploying REPLACES the rule's stream declarations, destinations and dataflows with this solution's, and keeps its immutable ID, so Abstract keeps sending without a change. Portal: Monitor > Settings > Data Collection Rules.

elements.name: dcrNameNew
elements.label: New rule name
elements.toolTip: What: the name of the new Data Collection Rule. Consequence: its immutable ID (an output of the deployment) is what you enter in Abstract as Data Collection Rule ID. 3 to 64 characters. When: a first install. Portal: Monitor > Settings > Data Collection Rules.

validations.message: 3 to 64 letters, digits, periods, underscores and hyphens.
A rule with this name is already in this resource group, and deploying would replace its streams, destinations and dataflows. Choose 'Use existing' to do that on purpose, or pick another name.

elements.name: dcrExisting
elements.label: Existing rule
elements.toolTip: What: the Data Collection Rules in this resource group, read live, each marked as an Abstract rule (it declares Custom-AbstractEventLogs_CL) or not. Consequence: the deployment replaces the rule's definition and keeps its immutable ID. When: re-running over a rule an earlier run created. Portal: Monitor > Settings > Data Collection Rules.

elements.name: customTablePlan
elements.label: Plan of AbstractEventLogs_CL
elements.toolTip: What: the Log Analytics table plan for the table that receives every Abstract event not routed elsewhere. When: keep Analytics if analytics rules or workbooks read it; Basic or Auxiliary only for search-only data. Consequence: Basic and Auxiliary stop this solution's analytics rules working on the table. 'Keep' never changes an existing table. Portal: Log Analytics workspace > Tables > AbstractEventLogs_CL > Manage table.

allowedValues.label: Keep (a new table starts on Analytics)
allowedValues.description: Never changes an existing table's plan. Safe default for a re-run.

allowedValues.label: Analytics
allowedValues.description: Full KQL, analytics rules, workbooks and hunting. Highest ingestion price.

allowedValues.label: Basic
allowedValues.description: Cheaper ingestion, limited KQL, no analytics rules. 30-day interactive retention.

allowedValues.label: Auxiliary (data lake)
allowedValues.description: Lowest price, searchable in the lake, no analytics rules or workbooks.

elements.defaultValue: Keep (a new table starts on Analytics)

elements.name: customTableRetentionDays
elements.label: Total retention of AbstractEventLogs_CL
elements.toolTip: What: how long AbstractEventLogs_CL keeps data, interactive and long-term together. When: leave 'Leave unchanged' to inherit the workspace default (or keep what an earlier run set). Consequence: longer retention is billed per GB per month after the included period. Portal: Log Analytics workspace > Tables > AbstractEventLogs_CL > Manage table.

allowedValues.label: Leave unchanged
allowedValues.description: The table keeps the retention it has now.

elements.name: enableDcrErrorLogs
elements.label: Record ingestion errors in DCRLogErrors
elements.toolTip: What: a diagnostic setting on the rule that writes transformation and ingestion errors to the DCRLogErrors table. When: keep it on; it is how you see an event the rule could not store. Consequence: a few rows per error, billed like any other Analytics data. Portal: the rule > Monitoring > Diagnostic settings.

options.text: ASIM (the Advanced Security Information Model) is Microsoft's common schema. Writing Abstract events into Microsoft's ASim tables means the ASIM analytics rules, hunting queries and workbooks already in the workspace see Abstract data with no change. Each schema adds one dataflow to the rule.

elements.name: enableAsim
elements.label: Write mapped events into Microsoft's ASIM tables
elements.toolTip: What: an extra route per chosen schema that maps matching events into that schema's ASim table. When: turn on if your SOC uses ASIM content or Microsoft solutions built on it. Consequence: expect new alerts from ASIM rules, and duplicates where a Microsoft connector already collects the same vendor. Portal: Log Analytics workspace > Tables, the ASim tables.

elements.name: asimSchemas
elements.label: ASIM schemas
elements.toolTip: What: the schemas to write, one ASim table each. Consequence: one dataflow per schema (Azure allows 20 per rule). When: keep all eight unless a Microsoft connector already fills a schema. Portal: Log Analytics workspace > Tables.

allowedValues.label: AuditEvent (ASimAuditEventLogs)
allowedValues.description: Configuration changes, admin actions and audit trails from any product Abstract normalises.

allowedValues.label: Authentication (ASimAuthenticationEventLogs)
allowedValues.description: Sign-ins, logons, MFA prompts and their failures. Feeds the identity analytics most SOCs rely on.

allowedValues.label: Dns (ASimDnsActivityLogs)
allowedValues.description: DNS queries and responses from resolvers, firewalls and secure-web gateways.

allowedValues.label: FileEvent (ASimFileEventLogs)
allowedValues.description: File create, modify, rename, delete and read events from EDR and file-integrity sources.

allowedValues.label: NetworkSession (ASimNetworkSessionLogs)
allowedValues.description: Firewall, flow and connection events. Usually the largest schema by volume.

allowedValues.label: ProcessEvent (ASimProcessEventLogs)
allowedValues.description: Process creation and termination from EDR and OS audit sources.

allowedValues.label: RegistryEvent (ASimRegistryEventLogs)
allowedValues.description: Windows registry key and value changes from EDR sources.

allowedValues.label: WebSession (ASimWebSessionLogs)
allowedValues.description: HTTP requests seen by proxies, WAFs and secure-web gateways.

elements.name: excludeAsimFromAbstractTable
elements.label: One copy: keep ASIM-mapped events out of AbstractEventLogs_CL
elements.toolTip: What: an event an ASIM route takes is stored once, in its ASim table, instead of twice. When: turn on to halve the ingestion of mapped events. Consequence: your own queries that read only AbstractEventLogs_CL stop seeing those events; this solution's analytics rules read both. Portal: Log Analytics workspace > Logs, query AbstractEventLogs_CL.

options.text: New workspace with ASIM: Microsoft Sentinel creates the ASim tables about two minutes after it is switched on. If the rule is created first, Azure refuses it with InvalidOutputTable. Open the failed deployment and select Redeploy with the same values; nothing that already succeeded changes.

The lake route sends events of the categories you choose to a table on the Auxiliary (data lake) plan instead of AbstractEventLogs_CL. Auxiliary is the cheapest plan: searchable with KQL, but analytics rules and workbooks do not run on it. Events an ASIM route takes never go to the lake.

elements.name: enableLake
elements.label: Send chosen categories to a data-lake table
elements.toolTip: What: one extra route to an Auxiliary-plan table. When: turn on for high-volume, low-alert data such as network flows. Consequence: those events leave AbstractEventLogs_CL, so analytics rules no longer see them. Portal: Log Analytics workspace > Tables.

elements.name: lakeTableName
elements.label: Lake table name
elements.toolTip: What: the Auxiliary-plan table that receives the chosen categories. Consequence: created if missing; an existing table must already be on the Auxiliary plan, because a table's plan cannot be switched to Auxiliary. Must end in _CL. Portal: Log Analytics workspace > Tables. When: change the name only if your naming standard needs it.

validations.message: A table name ending in _CL, such as AbstractLake_CL.

options.text: [concat(steps('lake').lakeTableName, ' already exists in this workspace on the ', coalesce(coalesce(steps('lake').lakeApi.properties, parse('{"plan":"","retentionInDays":0,"totalRetentionInDays":0}')).plan, ''), ' plan, ', string(coalesce(coalesce(steps('lake').lakeApi.properties, parse('{"plan":"","retentionInDays":0,"totalRetentionInDays":0}')).totalRetentionInDays, 0)), ' days total retention. [concat(steps('lake').lakeTableName, ' already exists on the ', coalesce(coalesce(steps('lake').lakeApi.properties, parse('{"plan":"","retentionInDays":0,"totalRetentionInDays":0}')).plan, ''), ' plan. A lake table must be on the Auxiliary plan and an existing table cannot be moved to it. Choose another name.')]

elements.name: lakeCategories
elements.label: Event categories for the lake
elements.toolTip: What: the Abstract event categories (event.category) sent to the lake. Matching contains the word, so 'network' also takes 'network_traffic'. Consequence: an event of a chosen category that an ASIM route also takes goes to the ASim table, not the lake. When: pick categories no analytics rule reads. Portal: Log Analytics workspace > Tables > the lake table.

allowedValues.label: network
allowedValues.description: Firewall, flow and connection events. The usual lake candidate: high volume, rarely alerted on.

allowedValues.label: web
allowedValues.description: Proxy and web-gateway traffic.

allowedValues.label: file
allowedValues.description: File activity.

allowedValues.label: process
allowedValues.description: Process activity.

allowedValues.label: authentication
allowedValues.description: Sign-ins and logons. Usually kept in Analytics for detections, not sent to the lake.

allowedValues.label: configuration
allowedValues.description: Configuration and change events.

allowedValues.label: iam
allowedValues.description: Identity and access management changes.

allowedValues.label: session
allowedValues.description: Session start and end events.

elements.name: lakeCategoriesOther
elements.label: Other categories
elements.toolTip: What: further categories, comma-separated, for values not in the list. When: leave empty unless your Abstract pipelines set their own event.category values. Consequence: a category nothing sets matches no events. Portal: your Abstract pipeline, field event.category.

elements.name: lakeRetentionDays
elements.label: Total retention of the lake table
elements.toolTip: What: how long the lake table keeps data. Consequence: lake storage is billed per GB per month; this sets the table's total retention. Portal: Log Analytics workspace > Tables > the table > Manage table. When: set it to your retention policy.

options.text: For each entry selected, the rule also writes the matching Abstract events into a Microsoft table: the vendor's own table (Okta and CrowdStrike with the transformation Microsoft publishes for that connector), CommonSecurityLog, Syslog, AWSCloudTrail, or an ASIM table. Install the vendor's solution from Content hub and its parsers, analytics rules and workbooks read Abstract-delivered data. The status of each vendor in the chosen workspace is read live below.

A new workspace has no vendor tables or solutions yet. The deployment creates each selected vendor's table; install the vendor's solution from Content hub afterwards.

elements.name: nativeVendors
elements.label: Vendor tables
elements.toolTip: What: the vendors whose own Sentinel table this rule also fills. When: pick a vendor whose Microsoft solution you use, or plan to. Consequence: one dataflow per vendor, and each event lands in exactly one vendor table: when several selected vendors match it, the first in this order takes it: asim-alert, okta, crowdstrike-hosts, aws-cloudtrail, csl-cef, csl-acs, syslog, asim-dhcp, asim-user-management. With store-once on (One copy, and Store each vendor event once), AbstractEventLogs_CL keeps only the events no vendor table, ASIM route or lake table takes; with it off, it also keeps every vendor event. Portal: Microsoft Sentinel > Content hub, the vendor's solution.

allowedValues.label: Okta: OktaV2_CL
allowedValues.description: Fills OktaV2_CL, the table Microsoft's Okta Single Sign-On solution reads, with Microsoft's own connector transformation.

allowedValues.label: CEF sources: CommonSecurityLog
allowedValues.description: Fills CommonSecurityLog, the table Microsoft's Common Event Format solution reads.

allowedValues.label: Cisco ASA, FortiGate and F5 ASM: CommonSecurityLog
allowedValues.description: Fills CommonSecurityLog, the table Microsoft's Common Event Format solution reads.

allowedValues.label: Syslog (Linux, Nutanix, Infoblox): Syslog
allowedValues.description: Fills Syslog, the table Microsoft's Syslog solution reads.

allowedValues.label: AWS CloudTrail: AWSCloudTrail
allowedValues.description: Fills AWSCloudTrail, the table Microsoft's Amazon Web Services solution reads.

allowedValues.label: CrowdStrike Falcon hosts: CrowdStrikeHostsV2_CL
allowedValues.description: Fills CrowdStrikeHostsV2_CL, the table Microsoft's CrowdStrike Falcon Endpoint Protection solution reads.

allowedValues.label: ASIM Alert (Abstract findings): ASimAlertEventLogs
allowedValues.description: Writes ASimAlertEventLogs, read by Microsoft's built-in ASIM parser.

allowedValues.label: ASIM DHCP: ASimDhcpEventLogs
allowedValues.description: Writes ASimDhcpEventLogs, read by Microsoft's built-in ASIM parser.

allowedValues.label: ASIM User Management: ASimUserManagementActivityLogs
allowedValues.description: Writes ASimUserManagementActivityLogs, read by Microsoft's built-in ASIM parser.

elements.name: oktaDomain
elements.label: Okta domain
elements.toolTip: What: your Okta org domain, written to the DomainName column of OktaV2_CL as Microsoft's own Okta connector does. When: set it when Okta is selected; empty leaves the column empty. Consequence: Microsoft's Okta content does not filter on it. Portal: the address you sign in to Okta with, without https://.

validations.message: A domain name such as example.okta.com: letters, digits, dots and hyphens.

elements.name: excludeNativeVendorsFromAsim
elements.label: Store each vendor event once
elements.toolTip: What: an event a vendor table takes is not also written to the ASim tables or the lake, and, with store-once on, not to AbstractEventLogs_CL. When: keep on, unless a report needs a second copy. Consequence: turned off, the same event is stored and billed in both tables and every search that unions them counts it twice. Portal: Log Analytics workspace > Tables.

options.text: [concat('This configuration gives the Data Collection Rule ', string(add(add(add(1, if(steps('asim').enableAsim, length(coalesce(steps('asim').asimSchemas, parse('[]'))), 0)), if(and(steps('lake').enableLake, not(empty(parse(if(empty(filter(split(replace(coalesce(steps('lake').lakeCategoriesOther, ''), ' ', ''), ','), (c) => not(empty(c)))), string(coalesce(steps('lake').lakeCategories, parse('[]'))), if(empty(coalesce(steps('lake').lakeCategories, parse('[]'))), string(filter(split(replace(coalesce(steps('lake').lakeCategoriesOther, ''), ' ', ''), ','), (c) => not(empty(c)))), replace(concat(string(coalesce(steps('lake').lakeCategories, parse('[]'))), string(filter(split(replace(coalesce(steps('lake').lakeCategoriesOther, ''), ' ', ''), ','), (c) => not(empty(c))))), '][', ','))))))), 1, 0)), length(coalesce(steps('vendors').nativeVendors, parse('[]'))))), ' of the 20 dataflows Azure allows: 1 for AbstractEventLogs_CL, one per ASIM schema, one for the lake and one per vendor.')]

The deployment always registers the Abstract package and its content templates, so Content hub lists them under 'Abstract Security for Microsoft Sentinel'. Choose which items to install now. Analytics and automation rules install disabled; enable them in Microsoft Sentinel when you are ready.

elements.name: abstractPkgNow
elements.visible: [not(empty(coalesce(first(filter(coalesce(steps('vendors').pkgApi.value, parse('[]')), (p) => equals(p.properties.displayName, 'Abstract Security for Microsoft Sentinel'))), parse('{"location":"","name":"","isAbstract":"no","properties":{"version":""}}')).properties.version))]

options.text: [concat('This workspace already has the Abstract package, version ', coalesce(coalesce(first(filter(coalesce(steps('vendors').pkgApi.value, parse('[]')), (p) => equals(p.properties.displayName, 'Abstract Security for Microsoft Sentinel'))), parse('{"location":"","name":"","isAbstract":"no","properties":{"version":""}}')).properties.version, ''), '. Deploying updates it in place; your own rules, workbooks and playbooks are not touched.')]

elements.name: deployDataConnectors
elements.label: Data connector tile
elements.toolTip: What: the 'Abstract Security (Security Data Pipeline)' tile in Microsoft Sentinel > Data connectors. Its status reads AbstractEventLogs_CL and Abstract rows in the ASim tables. Consequence: none on data; it only shows whether data is arriving. When: keep on unless you do not want the tile.

elements.name: deployParsers
elements.label: ASim_AbstractEvent parser
elements.toolTip: What: a workspace function that presents AbstractEventLogs_CL in ASIM shape. The hunting queries use it. Consequence: without it the hunting queries fail. Portal: Log Analytics workspace > Logs > Functions. When: keep on if you use the hunting queries.

elements.name: deployAnalyticsRules
elements.label: Analytics rules (3, installed disabled)
elements.toolTip: What: 'Abstract Security - High or Critical event', 'Abstract - Repeated auth failures followed by success' and 'Abstract Security - Finding' (findings from the asim-alert lane). They read AbstractEventLogs_CL and the ASim tables directly. Consequence: none until you enable them in Microsoft Sentinel > Analytics. When: keep on; enable the rules you want later.

elements.name: deployHuntingQueries
elements.label: Hunting queries (3)
elements.toolTip: What: 'Rare or newly-seen product', 'High cumulative-risk identities' and 'Daily value & reduction summary'. Portal: Microsoft Sentinel > Hunting > Queries. When: keep on. Consequence: none on data; queries run only when someone opens them.

elements.name: deployWorkbooks
elements.label: Workbooks: Pipeline Overview, Value & ROI
elements.toolTip: What: two workbooks on Abstract's pipeline volume, reduction and cost. Portal: Microsoft Sentinel > Workbooks > My workbooks. When: keep on. Consequence: none on data; opened on demand.

elements.name: deployDiscoveryWorkbook
elements.label: Workbook: Sentinel Discovery
elements.toolTip: What: a workbook that inventories the workspace's tables, connectors and ingestion so you can see what Abstract could take over. Portal: Microsoft Sentinel > Workbooks > My workbooks. When: keep on. Consequence: none on data; opened on demand.

elements.name: deployDiscovery
elements.label: Sentinel Discovery run (optional)
elements.toolTip: What: runs the read-only Sentinel inventory against this workspace from a managed identity and writes a report to a storage account in this resource group. When: turn it on if you want the report now; it adds read-only roles and runs for 5 to 15 minutes. Consequence: a new identity, storage account and two short container runs. Portal: Storage accounts > the absdisc account > Containers > sentinel-discovery.

elements.name: deployAutomationRules
elements.label: Automation rule: tag and prioritise Abstract incidents (disabled)
elements.toolTip: What: labels incidents raised by this solution's rules. Consequence: none until you enable it in Microsoft Sentinel > Automation. When: keep on; enable it later.

elements.name: deployPlaybooks
elements.label: Install the playbooks (Enrich incident, Verdict, Tune at source)
elements.toolTip: What: three Logic Apps that call the Abstract API from an incident: add Abstract context, ask for a verdict, and tune noisy sources at the pipeline. Each has a managed identity and a Microsoft Sentinel API connection. Consequence: they do nothing until run from an incident or an automation rule. Portal: Microsoft Sentinel > Automation > Active playbooks. When: keep on if you plan to use them; clear to install only the package and content.

elements.name: baseUrlChoice
elements.label: Abstract environment
elements.toolTip: What: which Abstract API the playbooks call. When: Abstract tells you if your tenant is elsewhere. Consequence: a wrong URL makes every playbook call fail. Portal: the URL you sign in to Abstract with.

elements.name: baseUrlOther
elements.label: Abstract API base URL
elements.toolTip: The HTTPS base URL Abstract gave you, without a trailing slash. What: the Abstract API base URL for the playbooks. When: only if Abstract gave you another environment. Consequence: every playbook call goes to this URL. Portal: Logic app > Parameters.

validations.message: An https:// URL with no path or trailing slash.

elements.name: abstractVendorAccountId
elements.label: Abstract vendor account ID
elements.toolTip: What: your Abstract tenant's vendor account ID, sent as x-as-vendor-account-id. When: leave empty to set it later on each playbook (Logic app > Parameters). Find it in Abstract under your account settings. Consequence: the Abstract API refuses calls without it, so the playbooks fail until it is set.
elements.placeholder: Leave empty to set it later

elements.name: kvMode
elements.label: Abstract API key in Key Vault
elements.toolTip: What: where the playbooks read the Abstract API key at run time. The key itself never enters this deployment. When: 'Pick a secret' lists vaults and their secrets; 'Enter the URI' for a vault you cannot list; 'Set later' leaves it empty. Consequence: until a secret is set, the playbooks fail at their first Abstract call. Portal: Key vaults > the vault > Objects > Secrets.

elements.name: kvSelector
elements.label: Key Vault
elements.toolTip: What: the vaults in your subscriptions that you can see. Pick the one that holds (or will hold) the Abstract API key. Consequence: none on the vault; the deployment does not change it. When: keep the API key in one vault you control. Portal: Key vaults.

elements.name: kvSecret
elements.label: Secret holding the Abstract API key
elements.toolTip: What: the vault's secrets, listed through Azure Resource Manager (names and URIs only; values are never read). Consequence: the playbooks read the latest version of this secret on every run, so rotating the key needs no redeploy. When: pick the secret that holds the Abstract API key. Portal: Key vault > Objects > Secrets.

constraints.allowedValues: [if(empty(coalesce(steps('playbooks').secretsApi.value, parse('[]'))), parse('[{"label":"No secrets in this vault (or no permission to list them)","value":""}]'), map(coalesce(steps('playbooks').secretsApi.value, parse('[]')), (s) => parse(concat('{"label":"', s.name, '","description":"', s.properties.secretUri, '","value":"', s.properties.secretUri, '"}'))))]

elements.name: kvUriManual
elements.label: Secret URI
elements.toolTip: What: the secret's URI with the Key Vault API version, as the playbooks call it. Find it: Key vault > Objects > Secrets > the secret > Secret Identifier, then add ?api-version=7.4. When: the vault cannot be listed from this form. Consequence: a wrong URI fails at the first Abstract call of each playbook.

options.text: After the deployment, give each playbook's managed identity 'Key Vault Secrets User' on the secret (Key vault > Objects > Secrets > the secret > Access control (IAM)) and 'Microsoft Sentinel Responder' on the workspace. The template creates no role assignments for the playbooks.

elements.name: lookbackHours
elements.label: Enrich-incident lookback
elements.toolTip: What: how far back the Enrich-incident playbook searches Abstract for related events. Consequence: a longer window finds more context and takes longer to run. When: 24 hours suits most SOCs. Portal: Logic app > Parameters.

elements.name: deployPlaybookAutomationRules
elements.label: Automation rules that run Verdict and Tune at source (disabled)
elements.toolTip: What: two automation rules that run the Verdict and Tune-at-source playbooks on new incidents. Consequence: the deployment FAILS unless Microsoft Sentinel's own app (Azure Security Insights) holds 'Microsoft Sentinel Automation Contributor' on this resource group, granted about 10 minutes earlier. The form checks for that role below. When: only after the role above has been granted. Portal: Microsoft Sentinel > Automation.

options.text: A 'Microsoft Sentinel Automation Contributor' assignment exists on this resource group. Make sure it is held by Azure Security Insights (app ID 98785600-1bb7-4fb9-b9fa-19afe2c8a360).

No 'Microsoft Sentinel Automation Contributor' assignment was found on this resource group, so this deployment would fail. Clear the box, or first run in Cloud Shell: az role assignment create --assignee 98785600-1bb7-4fb9-b9fa-19afe2c8a360 --role "Microsoft Sentinel Automation Contributor" --scope <this resource group's ID>, then wait about 10 minutes.
